subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. A wet heavy spiral turban shell with a knobbled whorl just lifted out of a coarse fishing net onto the plain iron platform of an 1860s submarine. Beyond it the narrow shoreline of the Keeling atoll is lined with coconut palms. Foreground shell and net clearly visible.
